categories.main_business_segments: Samsung Securities operates primarily in six business segments: brokerage (commission-based stock trading), corporate finance (including IPOs, M&A, and project financing), proprietary trading (stocks, bonds, derivatives), sales & trading (client fund-linked operations and institutional brokerage), futures brokerage, and overseas operations through subsidiaries. The company also engages in investment advisory, discretionary investment management, and trust services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced financial technologies including integrated risk management systems (SIRIS), proprietary derivative pricing engines, and digital asset management platforms. It employs sophisticated risk governance structures and quantitative risk measurement tools such as Value at Risk (VaR) and sensitivity analyses to manage market, credit, liquidity, and operational risks. Digital platforms support retail and institutional client services.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Samsung Securities serves a diverse customer base including retail investors, high-net-worth individuals (especially ultra-high-net-worth clients with assets over 3 billion KRW), institutional investors, and corporate clients. Its markets include domestic Korean capital markets and international markets via subsidiaries in the US, Europe, and Asia. The company targets asset management, brokerage, and investment banking clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in South Korea with a strong domestic presence through 28 branches nationwide. It also has overseas subsidiaries and offices in major financial centers including New York (USA), London (UK), Hong Kong, Tokyo (Japan), and Beijing (China), enabling it to serve global institutional investors and facilitate cross-border investment services.
categories.supply_chain_position: Samsung Securities operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the financial investment supply chain. It acts as an intermediary providing brokerage, investment advisory, asset management, and underwriting services, connecting capital providers (investors) with capital seekers (corporates and governments). It also engages in proprietary trading and risk management activities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses strategically on enhancing asset management capabilities, especially targeting the ultra-high-net-worth and affluent retail segments through personalized and digital asset management services. It emphasizes risk management innovation, ESG integration, and digital transformation to improve client experience and operational efficiency. R&D initiatives include advanced risk analytics, digital platforms, and expanding fee-based revenue streams.
categories.revenue_model: Samsung Securities generates revenue through multiple streams including brokerage commissions from stock and derivatives trading, investment banking fees from underwriting and advisory services, asset management fees from discretionary and advisory mandates, interest income from credit lending, and trust fees. It also earns income from proprietary trading and financial product sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include major Korean securities firms such as Mirae Asset Securities, NH Investment & Securities, KB Securities, Korea Investment & Securities, and Shinhan Investment Corp. Samsung Securities holds a leading position with a differentiated business model focused on affluent clients, diversified revenue sources, and strong institutional and international operations. It maintains competitive market shares in brokerage and investment banking.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, Samsung Securities reported total assets of approximately 56.5 trillion KRW, a 4.9% increase year-over-year, and equity of about 6.6 trillion KRW, up 6.9%. Net operating profit increased 17.6% to 1.647 trillion KRW, with net income attributable to controlling interests rising 29.6% to 547.4 billion KRW. The company’s ROE improved to 8.5%, reflecting solid growth and profitability in a competitive market.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Samsung Securities emphasizes its differentiated value through a strong affluent client base, leading asset management expertise, and comprehensive financial services tailored to client needs. It leverages advanced digital platforms and global networks to provide customized investment solutions and stable, diversified revenue streams. The company’s robust risk management and ESG commitment further enhance its competitive positioning and client trust.
